0.long_answer: A single benign tumor of the parathyroid gland is known as a parathyroid adenoma. This tumor is the most common cause of primary hyperparathyroidism. In primary hyperparathyroidism, the adenoma causes the affected parathyroid gland to produce excessive amounts of parathyroid hormone (PTH), leading to elevated calcium levels in the blood (hypercalcemia). Hypercalcemia can result in a variety of symptoms including kidney stones, bone pain, digestive issues, and psychiatric disturbances. Approximately 80-85% of primary hyperparathyroidism cases are due to a solitary parathyroid adenoma.
